title: Who are you, and what may you do?

sourceReferences.title: OWASP Authorization Cheat Sheet
sections: Validate the Permissions on Every Request
Verify that Authorization Checks are Performed in the Right Location

passages.title: Identity and permission
passages.text: Authentication establishes identity. Authorization decides whether a requested action is allowed. A successful sign-in does not grant access to every resource.

passages.title: 401 needs valid credentials
passages.text: A 401 response indicates that valid authentication credentials are missing for the target resource. The server must include a WWW-Authenticate challenge.

passages.title: 403 refuses the request
passages.text: A 403 response means the server understood the request but refuses it. Insufficient permission is one cause; 403 does not itself prove that the caller is authenticated. Repeating identical credentials need not resolve it.

passages.title: Two bearer-token failures
passages.text: For OAuth bearer tokens, an expired token is invalid_token and should receive 401. Insufficient token privileges are insufficient_scope and should receive 403. Token renewal and permission changes address different problems.

passages.title: Enforce access beyond the interface
passages.text: Validate permission for each request and the specific resource. Hiding a button can guide a user but cannot enforce access. The authoritative check belongs on the server, gateway or serverless function.

questions.prompt: Mai signs in to LearnSprint. The policy allows each learner to edit only their own notes. Does sign-in let Mai edit Bao's notes? Name the separate decision the API needs.

requiredIdeas: Authorize the edit against the note's ownership policy.
misconceptions: Being signed in permits all edits.

questions.prompt: GET /practice is protected by an HTTP authentication scheme. A client sends no credentials. Choose 401 or 403 and name the required response header.

requiredIdeas: WWW-Authenticate must supply an applicable challenge.

questions.prompt: An OAuth API accepts Linh's bearer token, but it contains only notes:read. DELETE /notes/7 needs notes:write. Choose the recommended HTTP status and bearer error. Would retrying the same token solve this?

requiredIdeas: No; the token lacks the required privilege.
misconceptions: Every failure involving a token requires token renewal.

questions.prompt: An OAuth bearer token has expired. The learner says, 'The token exists, so the failure must be 403.' Give the recommended status and bearer error, and explain the mistake.

requiredIdeas: An existing token can be expired and invalid.
misconceptions: Possessing any token proves valid authentication.

questions.prompt: A page hides the Edit button for another learner's note. Mai can still send a direct API request. What must the API decide before changing that note?

requiredIdeas: Check this caller's permission to edit this specific note.
A hidden button does not enforce the ownership rule.
misconceptions: The backend can trust the button's visibility.

questions.prompt: Two OAuth requests fail: A uses an expired token; B uses a valid token without the required scope. Match each to 401 or 403 and explain why the fixes differ.

requiredIdeas: A: 401; valid replacement credentials may help.
misconceptions: Replacing a token with unchanged privileges necessarily fixes B.

assessmentPolicy.correct: All required ideas are supported without a material contradiction.
assessmentPolicy.partial: Some required ideas are supported, but the explanation is incomplete or contains a limited error.
assessmentPolicy.incorrect: A substantive answer conflicts with the core concept.
assessmentPolicy.unable_to_assess: The response is blank, irrelevant or too unclear for a supported assessment; do not score it as incorrect.
